correctness.rationale: For the one-window update, normalize the sole residual secant or equivalently use its unnormalized least-squares coefficient t_j. Since AᵀA=SI and ⟨f,Af⟩=μ‖f‖², after an actual scalar step α_j the coefficient is 1−μ/(Sα_j). When α_j=β the correction vector Δx+βΔf equals βf_j, so the next step uses μ/S; after that step t_j=0 and the next step uses β. The initialization starts the induction. Both error-step matrices are nonsingular scaled rotations, so a nonzero initial error never vanishes and each secant is nonzero. They have norm factors z and r, giving the exact parity laws. Solving r²z²<1 gives the stated unique positive critical step; equality yields two fixed positive norm subsequences, and greater values give divergence. The unaccelerated norm factor z crosses 1 at 2μ/S; the threshold ratio and κ₂(A)=1 follow. At β=β_MR both steps coincide and every coefficient vanishes; the parity formulas still hold. In the cited Tang arXiv v1 the proper references are Algorithm 2.1 and limited-depth Proposition 2.7 (also Lemma 2.1), not the numbering in the frozen bibliography. Its window-one normalization matches the stated algorithm. The uploaded verifier and its recorded 486 and 605 checks were inspected, not executed. Its explicit threshold assertion compares β_crit with 2β_MR, rather than testing equality dynamics; the boundary conclusion follows from the algebra above.

evidence: For r_k=x_k−q(x_k), put Δr=r_k−r_(k−1) and w=r_k+γ_kΔr; least squares gives w⊥Δr. Smith's identity follows verbatim: r_(k+1)=Mw and MᵀM=z²I give ⟨r_(k+1),MΔr⟩=0 and ‖r_(k+1)‖²=⟨r_(k+1),Mr_(k−1)⟩. Hence whenever r_k=Mr_(k−1), r_(k+1) is orthogonal to r_(k+1)−r_k, making the next acceleration weight zero. This repeats from the ordinary first step.

In (2.5b), put I−M=βA. Then α(v)=μ/(βS) is independent of v. At odd k, γ_k=α−1; as q(x_(k−1))=x_k, the accelerated update is x_k+βα f_k. The two-step propagator is M[I−(μ/S)A], with norm factor zr; r_k=−βf_k has norm proportional to the error. Thus the full threshold, equality/divergence cases, and comparison with Richardson follow directly by solving zr<1 and z<1.

originality.rationale: The exact full-parameter formula is not printed in the inspected earlier sources, but it is mechanically implied by their combination. In exact arithmetic window-one AATGS is ordinary AA(1) on q(x)=(I−βA)x+βb. Adam Smith's 2024 thesis already proves the alternating-zero mechanism using only the scaled-orthogonality identity that this q satisfies. Once that mechanism is applied, the previously published two-step rAA(1) propagator of Krzysik–De Sterck–Smith applies with α(v)=μ/(βS) identically, yielding the other scalar step and norm multiplier by direct substitution. Smith also states the alternating coefficients, individual norm factors and rescued divergence window in the βμ=1 subfamily. The unrestricted positive-β critical value and advantage then use only the norm of a scaled rotation and a quadratic inequality. This is documented prior implication, not a negative verdict from an unavailable source or a claim that the frozen formulas are false.
residual_risks: The precise all-β threshold may also have been printed earlier, but the logical prior implication is enough without such a match.
